text:
eli: Hey team — customer (acct 8372) hit repeated 504/502s around 2026-03-15T14:05:22Z. They gave request_id: rqd_0a7f3c. I searched hot indices and got nothing, so I think this one is archived. Can someone outline exact steps to pull from archive and what to ask the customer for repro? :eyes:

maria: Likely archived indeed. Hot indices are 14 days, then rolled to cold snapshots retained for 1 year. Archive restore typically takes a few hours (2–6h) depending on shard. If older than 1y it may be purged; we'll confirm. KQL + lucene examples below to try first in case of partial hot data.

maria: KQL snippet (Kibana):
```
request_id:"rqd_0a7f3c" OR trace.id:"rqd_0a7f3c"
@timestamp:>= "2026-03-01T00:00:00Z" AND @timestamp:<= "2026-03-31T23:59:59Z"
```

maria: Lucene (Discover) fallback:
```
message:(rqd_0a7f3c) OR http.request_id:rqd_0a7f3c
```

jonathan: Internal fetch command we use for archive pulls (ops-only):
```
# runs retrieval job against archived shards for a given month
logctl fetch-archive --reqid rqd_0a7f3c --shard archived-2026-03 --out /tmp/rqd_bundle.gz
# returns job id and s3 path when done
```

ingrid: From support side, please ask the customer for: exact client timestamp (with timezone or UTC), full curl they used, response headers (very important), and the X-Request-Id they injected, if any. Example repro curl we can ask them to run: 
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDD_API_KEY" -H "X-Request-Id: rqd_0a7f3c" -d '{"input":"test"}' https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate
```

eli: I have their request body and the response body but they didn't include response headers or SDK debug logs. I'll ask them to re-run with -v or capture headers from their SDK.

maria: If they can enable SDK debug, ask for SDK logs (DEBUG=redwood:* or SDK debug flag). Also ask for HAR file if it's coming from a browser. Always request UTC times.

maria: Quick note on timezones: convert any local times to UTC before running queries; Kibana timestamps are stored as UTC.

eli: Can someone kick off the archive fetch? If ETA > 4h I'll tell customer 24–48h.

jonathan: Starting fetch now. Submitted logctl job 4591 against archived-2026-03 shard. ETA ~3h. I'll post s3 path when ready.

deploy-bot: job 4591 queued on archive-cluster shard archived-2026-03. ETA 3h.

ingrid: Thanks — Eli, once we have the bundle please grep for "error" and paste sanitized lines (no PII).

eli: Will do. Also requested response headers and SDK debug logs from the customer just now.

maria: If fetch fails due to retention or snapshot missing, fallback is cloud-provider snapshot restore (bigger escalation, 24–72h). We'll escalate to infra in that case.

jonathan: Update — job 4591 finished; bundle uploaded to s3://redwood-archives/4591/rqd_0a7f3c.tar.gz (internal access only).

eli: Downloading bundle now. Thanks.

ingrid: :thumbsup:

eli: Found relevant sanitized line in archive: 
```
[2026-03-15T14:05:22Z] request_id=rqd_0a7f3c status=502 upstream_error=ModelTimeout node=gpu-pool-4 latency_ms=1200
```

eli: Short analysis — upstream model-host timeout (node gpu-pool-4), latency spike ~1.2s. Looks transient. I'll offer customer a retry and explain it's a model-host timeout; I'll open infra ticket to check node health.

maria: Please open infra ticket referencing shard archived-2026-03 and attach the archive bundle and sanitized snippet. I'll monitor for regression.

eli: Opened INF-3321, attached bundle and pasted sanitized lines. I'll close the loop with the customer and offer retry/compensation as appropriate.

jonathan: If we see repeated hits to gpu-pool-4 for that time range, I'll add it to the node-health sweep.

eli: Closing here — thanks all for fast help. I'll update ticket and customer.
